rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha describes the Prophet moving her legs when he prostrated and her extending them again when he stood; Qurtubi treats this as direct contact without an intervening barrier.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء صريحا عنها قالت: «كنت أمد رجلي في قبلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that while searching for the Prophet at night in the mosque, her hand touched the soles of his feet as he prayed in prostration.
rows.anchor: وهو ما روته عائشة أيضا رضي الله عنها قالت: فقدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة من الفراش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports show that direct touch does not invalidate ablution for every person who touches; Qurtubi's rule distinguishes touch according to pleasure.
rows.anchor: كان دليلا على أن الوضوء لا ينتقض إلا على بعض الملامسين دون بعض

rows.speaker: المزني
rows.claim: Al-Muzani proposes that a barrier covered the Prophet's foot; Qurtubi rejects this because the default is direct contact unless a barrier is established.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: كان على قدمه حائل كما قاله المزنى

rows.speaker: الخصم
rows.claim: An opponent argues by consensus that forced intercourse without pleasure still obligates ghusl, so any touching or kissing should break ablution regardless of desire.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: فقد أجمعت الأمة على أن رجلا لو استكره امرأة فمس ختانه ختانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the alleged consensus is disputed because al-A'mash and others disagreed; even if granted, it begs the question, while sound reports support his position.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا أن الأعمش وغيره قد خالف فيما ادعيتموه من الإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi invokes the maxim to follow an authenticated report over one's own opinion, noting Malik, al-Shafi'i's teacher, was already known to say it.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الشافعي فيما زعمتم إنه لم يسبق إليه، وقد سبقه إليه شيخه مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the mere act of touching invalidates ablution would also make a man lose ablution by slapping his wife to discipline her, an implication Qurtubi says no one accepts.
rows.anchor: ويلزم على مذهبكم أن من ضرب امرأته فلطمها بيده تأديبا لها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet carried Umama, daughter of Zaynab, during prayer, setting her down for bowing and lifting her after prostration.
rows.anchor: كان يصلي وأمامة بنت أبي العاص ابنة زينب بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على عاتقه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: One Shafi'i opinion says touching even a little girl invalidates ablution based on the word “women”; Qurtubi rejects it, likening a child's touch to touching a wall.
rows.anchor: وهذا يرد ما قاله الشافعي في أحد قوليه: لو لمس صغيرة لانتقض طهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says pleasure is the criterion: wherever pleasure occurs, the ruling of required ablution follows; he contrasts this with al-Shafi'i's treatment of unmarriageable kin.
rows.anchor: واختلف قوله في ذوات المحارم لأجل أنه لا يعتبر اللذة، ونحن اعتبرنا اللذة فحيث وجدت وجد الحكم

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i limits legally relevant touch to the hand because that is the organ most commonly meant by the term; foot contact with a wife's private parts or belly would not invalidate ablution.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الأوزاعي في اعتباره اليد خاصة فلأن اللمس أكثر ما يستعمل باليد

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i says he would advise a man who asks about kissing his wife to renew ablution, but would not blame him if he did not.
rows.anchor: وقال في الرجل يقبل امرأته: إن جاء يسألني قلت يتوضأ، وإن لم يتوضأ لم أعبه

rows.speaker: أبو ثور
rows.claim: Abu Thawr holds that kissing, intimate contact, or touching one's wife does not require ablution; Qurtubi associates this with the Hanafi school.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: لا وضوء على من قبل آمرأته أو باشرها أو لمسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler may tayammum if water is entirely or partly unavailable, or seeking it risks losing companions or baggage, encountering thieves or beasts, missing prayer time, or causing thirst to oneself or another; cooking necessary food also counts.
rows.anchor: الأسباب التي لا يجد المسافر معها الماء هي إما عدمه جملة أو عدم بعضه، وإما أن يخاف فوات الرفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness counts when no one can hand over water or its use is feared harmful; a healthy resident may also lack usable water through widespread exorbitant prices, imprisonment, or restraint.
rows.anchor: ويترتب عدمه للمريض بألا يجد من يناوله، أو يخاف من ضرره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a person should buy water even by spending all his wealth and becoming destitute; Qurtubi calls this weak because religion is ease.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يشتري الرجل الماء بماله كله ويبقى عديما، وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: One group allows paying for water only up to a one-third increase over its ordinary price; another allows paying two or three times its value, positions Qurtubi says occur in Maliki law.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يشتريه ما لم يزد على القيمة الثلث فصاعدا. وقالت طائفة: يشتري قيمة الدرهم بالدرهمين والثلاث

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab says people should not be required to buy a water-skin for ten dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأشهب: أتشترى القربة بعشرة دراهم؟ فقال: ما أرى ذلك على الناس

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i rejects paying an increased price for water.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي بعدم الزيادة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik's apparent position, shared by al-Shafi'i, makes searching for water a condition for valid tayammum.
rows.anchor: فظاهر مذهب مالك أن ذلك شرط وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Qadi Abu Muhammad ibn Nasr hold that searching for water is not a condition of valid tayammum.
rows.anchor: وذهب القاضي أبومحمد بن نصر إلى أن ذلك ليس بشرط في صحة التيمم وهو قول أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly would not leave his travel route to seek water even when it lay two bowshots away; Ishaq says one need search only where one is.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أنه كان يكون في السفر على غلوتين من طريقه فلا يعدل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers requiring a search: the verse's “not finding water” presupposes looking, and a substitute is usable only when inability to obtain the original is certain.
rows.anchor: والأول أصح وهو المشهور من مذهب مالك في الموطأ لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When water seems impossible to find during the prayer time, tayammum and prayer early are recommended so the worshipper secures the virtue of praying early.
rows.anchor: فالأول يستحب له التيمم والصلاة في أول الوقت لأنه إذا فاتته فضيلة الماء

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: When water is likely to appear, Malik's companions report delaying prayer to mid-time in hope of water, provided the delay does not forfeit the virtue of praying early.
rows.anchor: الثاني يتيمم وسط الوقت حكاه أصحاب مالك عنه، فيؤخر الصلاة رجاء إدراك فضيلة الماء

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says that someone who knows water will be available at the end of the time may pray with tayammum early, but must repeat within the time if water later appears.
rows.anchor: فقد قال ابن القاسم: يجزئه، فإن وجد الماء أعاد في الوقت خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن حبيب
rows.claim: When the chances of finding water or not finding it are equal, delay prayer until the end of the chosen time because water's agreed virtue outweighs the disputed virtue of praying early; Ibn Habib identifies the endpoint.
rows.anchor: الثالث يؤخر الصلاة إلى أن يجد الماء في آخر الوقت لأن فضيلة الماء أعظم من فضيلة أول الوقت

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون
rows.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun says that if water is found later, the worshipper must repeat the prayer without time limitation.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: إن وجد الماء بعد أعاد أبدا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i in one opinion, and most scholars require enough water for the whole purification; less than the needed amount is treated as unavailable and is not used.
rows.anchor: والذي يراعى من وجود الماء أن يجد منه ما يكفيه لطهارته، فإن وجد أقل من كفايته تيمم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's other opinion requires using the water at hand and then performing tayammum for the part left without water, since the person initially possessed water.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي في القول: الآخر: يستعمل ما معه من الماء ويتيمم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: On forgetting water in one's baggage and using tayammum, al-Shafi'i's sounder view requires repeating because the water was present and the person was negligent; another view, also attributed to Malik, waives repetition if it was unknown.
rows.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي أيضا فيما إذا نسي الماء في رحله فتيمم والصحيح أنه يعيد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa permits ablution with water whose qualities have changed, arguing that the indefinite “water” in the verse is linguistically general.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة الوضوء بالماء المتغير لقوله تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi answers that the generality covers kinds within the genus of water, such as rain, rivers, springs, fresh, and salt water, not other liquids such as bean or rose water.
rows.anchor: ولكن في الجنس، فهو عام في كل ماء كان من سماء أو نهر أو عين عذب أو ملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that only nabidh is even discussed as a substitute drink for water in ablution or ghusl, but the verse's command to tayammum rules that substitution out.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن الوضوء والاغتسال لا يجوز بشيء من الأشربة سوى النبيذ عند عدم الماء

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: The report that Ibn Mas'ud performed ablution with nabidh is not established because its narrator Abu Zayd is unknown and not known as a companion of Abdullah, according to Ibn al-Mundhir and others.
rows.anchor: والحديث الذي فيه ذكر الوضوء بالنبيذ رواه ابن مسعود، وليس بثابت لأن الذي رواه أبو زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water whose absence permits tayammum is pure and purifying water that remains in its original qualities.
rows.anchor: الماء الذي يبيح عدمه التيمم هو الطاهر المطهر الباقي على أوصاف خلقته

rows.speaker: بعض من ألف في أحكام القرآن
rows.claim: A writer on Quranic rulings argues that because “water” is indefinite, tayammum is forbidden whenever any amount of water exists, mixed with other matter or alone.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض من ألف في أحكام القرآن لما قال تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء فتيمموا }

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans, including Abu Hanifa and his followers, argue that date nabidh counts as water and prevents tayammum; Qurtubi says their supporting reports are weak and treats the issue later in al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: ولا يمتنع أحد أن يقول في نبيذ التمر ماء فلما كان كذلك لم يجز التيمم مع وجوده

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the Muslim community was favored with three gifts, including making all earth a mosque and its soil a purifier; Qurtubi links the concession's revelation to the necklace incident.
rows.anchor: فضلنا على الناس بثلاث جعلت لنا الأرض كلها مسجدا وجعلت تربتها لنا طهورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, tayammum means intending or aiming: one aims at a thing or deliberately turns toward soil; usage later narrowed toward ritual wiping.
rows.anchor: التيمم لغة هو القصد. تيممت الشيء قصدته، وتيممت الصعيد تعمدته

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil rejects replacing tayammam with ammam in the cited verse because shazran means obliquely, from the side, rather than straight ahead.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: من قال في هذا البيت أممته فقد أخطأ لأنه قال «شزرا»

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays uses tayammam for heading toward a destination, in two poems about traveling toward a place and a spring.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: تيممتها من أذرعات وأهلها بيثرب أدنى دارها نظر عال

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses the verb for directing a camel toward another country when dissatisfied with the current land.
rows.anchor: آخر: إني كذاك إذا ما ساءني بلد يممت بعيري غيره بلدا

rows.speaker: أعشى باهلة
rows.claim: Al-A'sha of Bahila's verse uses tayammam for setting out toward Qays across difficult terrain.
rows.anchor: وقال أعشى باهلة: تيممت قيسا وكم دونه من الأرض من مهمه ذي شزن

rows.speaker: حميد بن ثور
rows.claim: Hamid ibn Thawr's verse uses the verb to ask where someone directed herself, illustrating its sense of intending or setting out.
rows.anchor: وقال حميد بن ثور: سل الربع أني يممت أم طارق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's verse says that wherever he aims, he carries his knowledge with him, another witness for tayammum as intention.
rows.anchor: وللشافعي رضي الله عنه: علمي معي حيثما يممت أحمله بطني وعاء له لا بطن صندوق

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit glosses the Quranic command as “aim” or “intend”; repeated usage then made the word denote wiping face and hands with soil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: قوله تعالى: { فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا } أي اقصدوا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains saying a man has tayammama as having wiped soil on his face and hands; Qurtubi identifies this as ritual tayammum when done as worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري في قولهم: «قد تيمم الرجل» معناه قد مسح التراب على وجهه ويديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two cited verses use mayammam for a person who directs himself toward a noble house, illustrating the word's sense of aiming or being directed.
rows.anchor:
إنا وجدنا أعصر بن سعد
ميمم البيت رفيع المجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tayammum occurs in al-Baqara, this sura, and al-Ma'ida; Qurtubi identifies the present verse as the tayammum verse.
rows.anchor: لفظ التيمم ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في «البقرة» وفي هذه السورة و «المائدة»

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi asks which of the two passages on tayammum Aisha meant when she said its verse was revealed, and observes that her report suggests the practice was previously unknown.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر ابن العربي: هذه معضلة ما وجدت لدائها من دواء عند أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi answers that Aisha meant this verse in al-Nisa, and agrees that tayammum was not known or practiced before its revelation, as historical accounts attest.
rows.anchor: قلت: أما قوله: «فلا نعلم أية آية عنت عائشة» فهي هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says ghusl for major ritual impurity was not prescribed before ablution, while historians agree the Prophet used ablution for prayer in Mecca; thus the new ruling then revealed was tayammum, not ablution.
rows.anchor: أنه معلوم عند جميع أهل السير أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منذ افترضت عليه الصلاة بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “the tayammum verse was revealed,” rather than “the ablution verse,” shows that the newly taught rule was tayammum; the ablution obligation already existed and was now recited in revelation.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل آية الوضوء ما يبين أن الذي طرأ لهم من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum is obligatory for every accountable person owing prayer when water is absent and prayer time has entered.
rows.anchor: التيمم يلزم كل مكلف لزمته الصلاة إذا عدم الماء ودخل وقت الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, his two companions, and al-Muzani allow tayammum before the prayer time because searching for water is not a condition, analogizing to voluntary prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وصاحباه والمزني صاحب الشافعي: يجوز قبله لأن طلب الماء عندهم ليس بشرط

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Dharr that clean earth is a Muslim's purification even without water for ten years; the opposing jurists treat this as equating soil purification with water ablution.
rows.anchor: الصعيد الطيب وضوء المسلم ولو لم يجد الماء عشر حجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi argues that “not finding water” means one must first seek it, and tayammum is a necessity purification like that of a woman with continuous bleeding.
rows.anchor: ودليلنا قوله تعالى: { فلم تجدوا مآء } ولا يقال: لم يجد الماء إلا لمن طلب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The rule to perform tayammum and pray wherever prayer catches a person is al-Shafi'i's and Ahmad's view, and is also reported from Ali, Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الشافعي وأحمد، وهو مروي عن علي وابن عمر وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that tayammum does not remove major or minor ritual impurity; finding water restores the person to the prior state, based on the Prophet's instruction to Abu Dharr to let water touch his skin.
rows.anchor: وأجمع العلماء على أن التيمم لا يرفع الجنابة ولا الحدث

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama reportedly says a junub person who finds water after tayammum remains purified and needs neither ghusl nor ablution until a new occurrence.
rows.anchor: إلا شيء روي عن أبي سلمة بن عبدالرحمن، رواه ابن جريج وعبد الحميد بن جبير بن شيبة عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr calls Abu Salama's reports contradictory and poorly considered, adding that Abu Salama was not as learned as his Medinan Successor peers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: وهذا تناقض وقلة روية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is agreement that finding water before beginning prayer invalidates tayammum and requires using the water.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن من تيمم ثم وجد الماء قبل الدخول في الصلاة بطل تيممه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that a completed prayer after diligent water-search remains valid even if water is then found; some recommend repeating within the time after ablution or ghusl.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن من تيمم وصلى وفرغ من صلاته، وقد كان اجتهد في طلبه الماء

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus, Ata, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Makhul, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, and Rabi'a all say that a person who finds water after the prayer repeats it.
rows.anchor: وروي عن طاووس وعطاء والقاسم بن محمد ومكحول وابن سيرين والزهري وربيعة كلهم يقول

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In the report of Abu Said, two travelers pray after tayammum; the Prophet says the one who does not repeat followed the Sunna and the one who repeats earns double reward.
rows.anchor: لما رواه أبو سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: Abu Dawud transmits the two-traveler report and notes that the Abu Said link is not preserved in other narrations; al-Daraqutni's version specifies finding water within the prayer time.
rows.anchor: أخرجه أبو داود وقال: وغير ابن نافع يرويه عن الليث عن عميرة بن أبي ناجية

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: If water appears during prayer, Malik says not to interrupt: complete the prayer and use water for later prayers; al-Shafi'i and Ibn al-Mundhir agree, while Abu Hanifa, Ahmad, al-Muzani, and others require stopping and restarting.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: ليس عليه قطع الصلاة واستعمال الماء وليتم صلاته وليتوضأ لما يستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi cites “do not invalidate your works” as support for completing a prayer begun validly with tayammum; no Sunna or consensus requires cutting it when water appears.
rows.anchor: ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy, someone fasting most of an expiation fast does not discard it upon finding an enslaved person to free; likewise, one who began prayer with tayammum completes it.
rows.anchor: أن من وجب عليه الصوم في ظهار أو قتل فصام منه أكثره ثم وجد رقبة لا يلغي صومه

rows.speaker: شريك بن عبد الله القاضي
rows.claim: Sharik ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi requires a new tayammum for every prayer, voluntary or obligatory.
rows.anchor: فقال شريك بن عبدالله القاضي: يتيمم لكل صلاة نافلة وفريضة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik requires a separate tayammum for each obligatory prayer because the worshipper must seek water anew for each one.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: لكل فريضة لأن عليه أن يبتغي الماء لكل صلاة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, al-Layth, Hasan ibn Hayy, and Dawud allow as many prayers as desired with one tayammum until ritual impurity occurs.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والثوري والليث والحسن بن حي وداود: يصلي ما شاء بتيمم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers a new tayammum for each prayer: God requires seeking water for each prayer, and tayammum is an incomplete necessity-purity that consensus says ends when water appears.
rows.anchor: وما قلناه أصح لأن الله عز وجل أوجب على كل قائم إلى الصلاة طلب الماء

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and the first group disallow tayammum before prayer time because the verse links it to a need that does not exist before the time.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا لا يصلى فرضين بتيمم واحد، وهذا بين

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: One transmission from Ibn al-Qasim says the second of two obligatory prayers performed with one tayammum must be repeated while its time remains.
rows.anchor: فروى يحيى بن يحيى عن ابن القاسم: يعيد الثانية ما دام في الوقت

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: A transmission from Ibn al-Qasim through Abu Zayd, and reports from Mutarrif and Ibn al-Majishun, require repeating the second prayer forever because seeking water is a condition.
rows.anchor: وكذلك روي عن مطرف وابن الماجشون يعيد الثانية أبدا

rows.speaker: أبو الفرج
rows.claim: Abu al-Faraj permits making up multiple missed prayers with one tayammum; this assumes water-search is not a condition, which Qurtubi rejects.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفرج فيمن ذكر صلوات: إن قضاهن بتيمم واحد فلا شيء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi cites 18:8, describing barren ground, to illustrate ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface.
rows.anchor: أي أرضا غليظة لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi explains ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface and traces its name to being the upper limit to which one rises.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي صعيدا لأنه نهاية ما يصعد إليه من الأرض

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses ṣaʿīd for the ground, describing an insect striking it with its snout.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول ذي الرمة: كأنه بالضحى ترمي الصعيد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿīd has the plural ṣaʿidat; the hadith warning against sitting in public roads uses that plural.
rows.anchor: وجمع الصعيد صعدات ومنه الحديث

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and al-Tabari allow tayammum on any part of the earth, including soil, sand, stones, minerals, or saline ground; here ṭayyib means pure.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة: يتيمم بوجه الأرض كله ترابا كان أو رملا أو حجارة أو معدنا أو سبخة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group interprets ṭayyib as lawful, a reading Qurtubi calls strained.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: «طيبا» حلالا وهذا قلق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Yusuf restrict ṣaʿīd to fertile, growing soil and read ṭayyib as good soil, citing the verse that good land yields plants; al-Shafi'i requires dusty soil.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأبو يوسف: الصعيد للتراب المنبت وهو الطيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that cultivated earth is the best ṣaʿīd; Abu Umar says this implies ṣaʿīd can also refer to earth that is not cultivated.
rows.anchor: وذكر عبدالرزاق عن ابن عباس أنه سئل أي الصعيد أطيب؟ فقال الحرث

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says ṣaʿīd means soil specifically.
rows.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: هو التراب خاصة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil's lexicon, as cited by Ibn Faris, glosses tayammum with ṣaʿīd as taking its dust, implying soil because smooth stone has no dust.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب الخليل: تيمم بالصعيد، أي خذ من غباره حكاه ابن فارس

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari says al-Shafi'i requires dust to adhere to the hand and be transferred to the body parts, analogizing earth to water; he admits ṣaʿīd alone does not prove this restriction.
rows.anchor: واشترط الشافعي أن يعلق التراب باليد ويتيمم به نقلا إلى أعضاء التيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects treating the hadith naming soil as a restriction on the general earth term, comparing it to a verse that names dates and pomegranates among fruits.
rows.anchor: إنما هو من باب النص على بعض أشخاص العموم كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi's analogy also points to the al-Baqara verse listing angels, messengers, Gabriel, and Michael, where naming examples does not restrict the broader class.
rows.anchor: وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣaʿīd means the earth's surface, it is a place where tayammum is performed; if it means soil, it is the direct object with an omitted preposition, and ṭayyib is its adjective or, in the lawful reading, an adverbial or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: ف «صعيدا» على هذا ظرف مكان. ومن جعله للتراب فهو مفعول به بتقدير حذف الباء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells a junub person to use ṣaʿīd because it suffices; Qurtubi cites this to support the earth-surface interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم للجنب: «عليك بالصعيد فإنه يكفيك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consensus case for tayammum is clean, fertile soil that has not been moved or usurped; consensus bars gold, silver, gems, food, and impure substances.
rows.anchor: مكان الإجماع مما ذكرناه أن يتيمم الرجل على تراب منبت طاهر غير منقول ولا مغصوب

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik and others allow tayammum on minerals, while al-Shafi'i and others prohibit it.
rows.anchor: واختلف في غير هذا كالمعادن فأجيز وهو مذهب مالك وغيره. ومنع وهو مذهب الشافعي وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says Malik permits tayammum on grass if it lies beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن خويز منداد: ويجوز عند مالك التيمم على الحشيش إذا كان دون الأرض

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Maliki sources differ on snow: the Mudawwana and al-Mabsut allow it, while other sources prohibit it.
rows.anchor: واختلف عنه في التيمم على الثلج ففي المدونة والمبسوط جوازه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most jurists prohibit tayammum on wood, though Mukhtasar al-Waqqar allows it; one view distinguishes attached from detached wood.
rows.anchor: واختلف المذهب في التيمم على العود فالجمهور على المنع

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri allow tayammum on earth and everything on it, including trees, stones, rocks, ice, and snow; al-Tha'labi attributes to Malik permission to strike a tree and wipe with the hand.
rows.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي والثوري: يجوز بالأرض وكل ما عليها من الشجر والحجر والمدر وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says most Malikis allow tayammum on moved soil, though a Maliki minority forbids it; baked lime and brick have two views, and the wall is disputed.
rows.anchor: وأما التراب المنقول من طين أو غيره فجمهور المذهب على جواز التيمم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the Bukhari-transmitted report of the Prophet wiping on a wall proves tayammum is valid without soil, supporting Malik over al-Shafi'i.
rows.anchor: أخرجه البخاري. وهو دليل على صحة التيمم بغير التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the wall report proves tayammum is valid without soil, against al-Shafi'i's requirement for pure, adherent dust.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل على صحة التيمم بغير التراب كما يقوله مالك ومن وافقه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that Ibn Ulayya and Ibn Kaysan permit tayammum with musk or saffron; Ibn Atiyya calls this completely mistaken.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن ابن علية وابن كيسان أنهما أجازا التيمم بالمسك والزعفران

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar says the scholars generally allow tayammum on saline ground, with Ishaq ibn Rahawayh the exception.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وجماعة العلماء على إجازة التيمم بالسباخ إلا إسحاق بن راهويه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person who reaches the point of tayammum while in mud should coat part of the body with mud and, once dry, use it for tayammum.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس فيمن أدركه التيمم وهو في طين قال يأخذ من الطين فيطلي به بعض جسده

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri and Ahmad permit tayammum with dust from felt.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري وأحمد: يجوز التيمم بغبار اللبد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi says Abu Hanifa permits tayammum with kohl, arsenic, lime, gypsum, and powdered gems, but not metal filings because they are not of the earth's genus.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة التيمم بالكحل والزرنيخ والنورة والجص والجوهر المسحوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masḥ can mean intercourse, cutting with a sword, a camel's day's travel, a woman without buttocks, or a touch of beauty; here it means dragging the hand across the object.
rows.anchor: المسح لفظ مشترك يكون بمعنى الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When wiping is done with an instrument, the hand carries and moves that instrument across the surface being wiped.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا بالمسح عبارة عن جر اليد على الممسوح خاصة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i reads “from it” in al-Ma'ida as requiring soil to be transferred to the limbs; Qurtubi and Malik do not require transfer because the Prophet struck the ground, lifted and blew or shook his hands, and also wiped on a wall.
rows.anchor: فقوله «منه» يدل على أنه لا بد من نقل التراب إلى محل التيمم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i analogizes tayammum to wiping the head: just as water must be carried to the head, soil must be carried to the limbs.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي: لما لم يكن بد في مسح الرأس بالماء من بلل ينقل إلى الرأس

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلمة
rows.claim: There is no dispute that the whole face must be covered in ablution and tayammum; some exempt folds and spaces between fingers, a position in the Maliki school attributed to Muhammad ibn Maslama by Ibn Atiyya.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن حكم الوجه في التيمم والوضوء الاستيعاب وتتبع مواضعه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority follow the verse's order, wiping the face before the hands; a report in al-Bukhari's chapter on one-strike tayammum mentions the hands first, as do some scholars by analogy with reversing ablution order.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالوجه قبل اليدين وبه قال الجمهور

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab says the hand wipe reaches the shoulders, a position also reported from Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن شهاب: إلى المناكب. روي عن أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: A report from al-A'mash in Abu Dawud's Musannaf says the Prophet wiped to the middle of his forearms; Ibn Atiyya says he knew of no one who followed this report.
rows.anchor: وفي مصنف أبي داود عن الأعمش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مسح إلى أنصاف ذراعيه
